translation:
  text: '“Those who handed in green rods whose very tips were dry and cracked have always been good, faithful
    and honored in God’s sight. They sinned very little, through small desires and minor grievances against
    one another. But after hearing my words, most quickly repented, and their dwelling came to be in the
    tower.”


    2. “Some of them wavered, and some who wavered caused greater division. There is still hope of repentance
    for these, because they have always been good. Hardly any of them will die.”[a]


    3. “Those who handed in dry rods with only a little green are people who only believed, while doing
    lawless deeds.[b] They never turned away from God. They gladly bore the name and gladly welcomed God’s
    servants into their homes. On hearing of this repentance, they repented without hesitation and now
    practice every virtue and righteousness.”[c]


    4. “Some of them will also suffer, recognizing the deeds they have done.[d] All of these will have
    their dwelling in the tower.”'
  philosophy: optimal-equivalence
  footnotes:
  - marker: a
    reason: lexical_alternative
    text: “Hardly any of them will die” renders the working Greek’s difficult/unlikely expression; it
      is not a guarantee that none can die. The hope of repentance and the account of wavering and division
      remain explicit.
  - marker: b
    reason: textual_variant
    text: '“Only believed” follows the bounded Athos reading monon, printed in Lake (1907), Plate X line
      6 and reported in the 1891 apparatus, rather than its conjectural men. Alternative: “They are people
      who believed, but did lawless deeds.” Michigan’s corresponding word is wholly restored from line
      spacing in Bonner printed p. 112, not preserved ink. The draft does not turn the phrase into a later
      doctrinal slogan or deny the source’s following statement that they had not turned away from God.'
  - marker: c
    reason: textual_variant
    text: '“Every virtue and righteousness” retains the working Athos construction. Michigan’s published
      wording has a different virtue/righteousness construction, with letters supplied at the break; the
      versions also vary. Alternative sense: “They practice every virtue of righteousness.” No independent
      certification of the entire restored papyrus phrase is claimed.'
  - marker: d
    reason: textual_variant
    text: “Will also suffer” carries forward the existing bounded Michigan pathountai selection; the word
      itself is outside restoration brackets in Bonner printed p. 113. Present sense “also suffer” is
      possible. Athos has “are also afraid”; the 1891 body conjectures “suffer willingly.” The papyrus’s
      following gladly/suffer phrase is an editorial restoration from Latin and is not adopted as preserved
      Greek. No willingness is added to this English selection.
lexical_decisions:
- source_word: μετάνοια / διψυχεῖν
  chosen: repentance / waver
  alternatives:
  - turning back / be double-minded
  rationale: Keep the concrete change of deeds, conditions and warnings. Do not erase the difference between
    an opportunity to repent and its actual acceptance.
- source_word: παθοῦνται
  chosen: will suffer
  alternatives:
  - suffer
  - are afraid (Athos)
  - suffer willingly (1891 conjecture)
  rationale: Carry forward the declared Michigan verb without importing the adjacent modern restoration
    as preserved willingness.
